title: Calibrate the singulion ordering objective on the Aberdeen Bestiary
statement: In the published medieval Latin control, fixed-orientation cosine maximization recovered the conventional nested order in 9 of 10 usable quires with a full-book 75-dimensional TF-IDF fit. It recovered all five known orders of virtual sheets made from successive pairs of folios. With page-aligned fitting these counts were 8 of 10 and 5 of 5. When each entire test quire was removed from vocabulary estimation and SVD training, they fell to 3 of 10 and 1 of 5. All outcomes come from exact enumeration within one layout at a time. This shows ordering power within this control and the cost of projecting to a space fitted on other quires. It gives no verdict about how the Voynich bifolia were produced or assembled.
check: Reproduce the two order-control tasks in Layfield and Davis's other known-text benchmark, the Speculum. Freeze preprocessing, known orientations, candidate geometry and training access before scoring. Report percentile in the exact permutation distribution and identifiable order recovery. Keep all nested geometry comparisons on the same objective and compare a stack candidate to a separately enumerated stack distribution.

citations.locus: Layfield and Davis 2026, paras. 21–30, Tables 3, 6, 14–15, appendix on same-corpus fitting
Aberdeen University MS 24, Latin text is under Transcription and Translation
Editorial notation for supplements and variants
Author-uploaded Timm paper, §§4–5, particularly the proposed permuted known-text check

methods:
Layfield and Davis (2026), paras. 21–30 and Tables 3 and 6, report latent semantic associations for the Aberdeen Bestiary. Their exhaustive resequencing test is applied to two Voynich quires in paras. 50–54 and Tables 14–15. Timm's methodological review §§4–5 asks for a known-text order calibration and separate within-candidate permutation variation. I applied those checks to the public medieval Latin control. No Voynich text or page selection is used in this experiment.

The University of Aberdeen publishes both a Latin transcription and an English translation for each available MS 24 page. Fetch the official HTML for f1r–f94v. Take Latin from the Transcription div alone. Discard bracketed conjectures and witness variants identified in the edition's help page. Join a backslash where it occurs directly between letters, remove the other line break markers, lowercase, normalize accents and retain sequences of ASCII letters. This gives 181 text faces and 39,765 tokens, with a compact frozen Latin function-word list used for the modeling step. In seven cases the capture supplies no Latin for our parser, including f45r, whose corresponding translation remains available. Quire 7 is excluded because f45r is one of its needed faces. Only paired leaves in the paper's collation table are used. Singletons and omitted leaves follow the published pairing table.

The main model uses a term matrix of consecutive 40-word excerpts from the concatenated Latin, smooth TF-IDF, a minimum of two excerpt occurrences, 75-dimensional SVD and page fold-in through the fitted right singular vectors. Matrices are L2-normalized before taking cosine. Sensitivity checks apply log-entropy weights, direct full-dimensional TF-IDF cosine, and a 40-token physical-edge comparison. A further in-book fit ends each training chunk at the page boundary and accepts final chunks of 20–39 words. The whole-quire exclusion uses this latter fit and removes the complete range of the test quire from vocabulary estimation and embedding training. All required evaluation pages are still projected as queries. This is an independent approximation to the paper. Its source preprocessing and corpus sizes differ, and values are not intended to numerically duplicate Table 6.

The conventional nesting is the published physical pairing and current verified folio sequence. Fix the orientation of every sheet. For a placement permutation take the ascending, first side of each sheet and then close out with the second sides in reverse order. Average the cosine of every next-leaf pair from a verso to a recto, including the middle opening. The second test constructs artificial contiguous 4-page blocks from two successive folios in each complete eight-leaf quire. Their true order is the known bound text order by construction. Permute intact blocks and average only the cosine across block boundaries. In both tests compare the observed order with the entire distribution computed using the same feasible moves and same objective. The search result is invariant to the order in which candidate permutations are presented. The two geometry-specific scores have different numbers of transitions and are kept on separate scales.

The synthetic controls use four ordered four-page blocks with 220 draws per page. An independent sample draws only from the same 96 background types. In the lexical-bridge sample, the facing pair at each true block boundary shares its own eight-type pool that accounts for 52 of each page's 220 tokens. Permuting page identities tests the bridges under a broken reference. Sixty-four fixed seeds per condition were scored on direct raw count cosine, with the same set of 24 candidate orders and an absolute 1e-10 tolerance for ties. They show the magnitude of optimization gain on these controls, without modeling a specific scribe.
additional_findings: Using raw full-dimensional TF-IDF cosine gives 8/10 physical nests and 3/5 contiguous stacks. Log-entropy SVD gives 8/10 and 5/5. Keeping only 40 tokens either side of each opening gives 9/10 and 5/5 under the main fit.

The all-text fit admits a median 57.3% of test-face tokens into the model vocabulary. With the quire excluded, median coverage is 43.6%. Thus the stronger test changes exposure to topical and lexical material as well as preventing in-sample fitting.

The main five intact contiguous stacks each have 24 permutations. The across-quire median of the maximum minus the permutation median is 0.201 cosine in this test. Controls show that positive gains can arise even if the reference order is meaningless. Several real ranks are clearly distinguished while in-book, so positive improvements do not on their own show either useful recovery or failure.

The toy positive recovers 39/64 exact reference orders, the identity-shuffled version 0/64 and the independent bag reference 2/64. The simulated maximizer still exceeds the permutation median in both negative panels. These nominal 64 runs per panel serve as controls for the objective, not empirical material estimates.
token_hash_definition: SHA-256 of numeric folio order with recto first: each nonempty page label, TAB, joined normalized tokens, LF.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.8, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and threadpoolctl.
reproduction.instructions: Write the script strings to four files in one scratch directory. Run download, calibrate, sensitivity and toy in that order. Download fetches the official public edition and preserves captures in a pages subdirectory.

scripts.download.py:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from threading import Lock
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

base=Path(__file__).parent
directory=base/'pages'
directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
gate=Lock()
last=0
labels=[f'{n}{side}' for n in range(1,95) for side in 'rv']
def fetch(label):
    global last
    target=directory/f'{label}.html'
    if target.exists():
        return 'cached'
    for attempt in range(3):
        with gate:
            time.sleep(max(0,.25-(time.monotonic()-last)))
            last=time.monotonic()
        url=f'https://www.abdn.ac.uk/bestiary/ms24/f{label}'
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url,timeout=12) as response:
                document=response.read()
            target.write_bytes(document)
            return 'downloaded'
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            if exc.code==404:
                print(label,'not available',flush=True)
                return 'missing'
            if attempt==2:
                print(label,'HTTP',exc.code,flush=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            if attempt==2:
                print(label,exc,flush=True)
        time.sleep(.7)
    return 'failed'
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
    counts={}
    for val in pool.map(fetch,labels):
        counts[val]=counts.get(val,0)+1
print(counts,flush=True)
scripts.toy.py:
from itertools import permutations
import json
from statistics import median
import numpy as np
from calibrate import BASE, plan_rank
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits

ref = (0, 1, 2, 3)
orders = list(permutations(ref))
def ends(order):
    return [(a * 4 + 3, b * 4) for a, b in zip(order, order[1:])]

outputs = {}
with threadpool_limits(limits=2):
    for mode in ('bridge', 'shuffled_page_identity', 'iid_background'):
        runs = []
        for seed in range(64):
            rng = np.random.default_rng(408 + seed)
            counts = rng.multinomial(220, np.repeat(1/96, 96), size=16)
            total = np.pad(counts, ((0,0),(0,24)))
            if mode != 'iid_background':
                for j in range(3):
                    for i in (4*j+3, 4*j+4):
                        total[i,:96] = rng.multinomial(168, np.repeat(1/96,96))
                        total[i,96+j*8:104+j*8] = rng.multinomial(52,np.repeat(1/8,8))
            if mode == 'shuffled_page_identity':
                total = total[rng.permutation(len(total))]
            x = total / np.linalg.norm(total, axis=1)[:,None]
            matrix = x @ x.T
            def score(order):
                return sum(float(matrix[a,b]) for a,b in ends(order))/3
            r = plan_rank(ref,orders,score,ends)
            runs.append(r)
        outputs[mode] = {
            'n': len(runs),
            'unique_maximum': sum(not r['better_count'] and r['optima']==1 for r in runs),
            'median_reference_rank': median(r['better_count']+1 for r in runs),
            'median_gold_score': median(r['ref_score'] for r in runs),
            'median_maximum': median(r['max'] for r in runs),
            'median_gain_over_median': median(r['max']-r['median'] for r in runs),
        }
(BASE / 'toy.json').write_text(json.dumps(outputs,indent=2)+'\n')
